summary: A 1932 steel tower that doubled as a WWII aircraft-spotting post, now standing in Milan Hill State Park and climbable to the deck below the cab.

facts.design: 45' steel tower with standard NH wooden cab

access.note: Inside Milan Hill State Park; visitors can climb to the observation deck just below the cab.

facts.agency: NH Division of Forests and Lands

events.note: 45-foot steel tower with standard NH wooden cab; used as a WWII aircraft-spotting station
Registered March 12, 2002, as US 412 / NH 13, nominated by NH registrar Chris Haartz

notes_for_editor: The tower's own NHLR page is rich (built year, design, WWII use, administering/cooperating agencies, nomination, and a 2019 field inspection with staffing/condition detail), but outside corroboration is thinner than the 'well-documented' label implied: Wikipedia and the state park site confirm 1932 and public access but add little else, and a promising newspaper piece (Conway Daily Sun, 'Milan Hill's fire tower is 1 of 15 still in use') returned HTTP 429 on every fetch attempt and was never read -- worth another try, it likely has more on current staffing and may confirm or refute a claim (surfaced only in AI-synthesized web-search summaries, not in any page actually read) that the 1932 tower replaced an earlier one on nearby Jodrie Hill. I left that claim out of the story entirely since I couldn't verify it against a primary source. On location: the record's existing lat/lon (from ffla) is corroborated by OpenStreetMap's independently mapped tower node, while the NHLR page's own stated coordinates sit about 1.65 km (roughly a mile) away -- this likely resolves the 'conflicts' entry already in the tower record in ffla's favor, though I'm not proposing a formal correction since the record's location field already uses the better-supported value. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the CCC-camp sentence was footnoted to the state park page, which does not mention the CCC at all; moved that citation to Wikipedia, which does state it. Also corrected the story's claim that the NHLR/FFLA coordinates differ by 'a mile and a half' -- the actual gap (1,653 m) is about one mile, not 1.5. Used 2 of 3 allotted WebSearch calls (research); fact-check pass used WebFetch only, no WebSearch.
